blocks.prompt: 8 Find the square root of \(13 - 20\sqrt{3}i\) and represent them on an Argand diagram.
blocks.explanation:
Two jobs: find the two square roots (as in Question 7), then plot them.
Plan: \(|z|\), then \(p\) and \(q\), choose signs, check, and plot each root \(a + ib\) as the point \((a, b)\).
steps:
Given: \(z = 13 - 20\sqrt{3}i\).
To find: both square roots, shown on an Argand diagram.
Method: Square-root formula (Section 1.2.1) with \(p = \sqrt{\frac{|z| + x}{2}}\) and \(q = \sqrt{\frac{|z| - x}{2}}\): \(\sqrt{z} = \pm(p + iq)\) if \(y > 0\), \(\pm(p - iq)\) if \(y < 0\). This fits because the formula gives the square roots of any \(x + iy\) directly.

Read off \(x\) and \(y\)
\[x = 13,\quad y = -20\sqrt{3} < 0\]
Why: Write the number as \(x + iy\); the sign of \(y\) will decide the signs of the answer.

Work out \(p\)
\[p = \sqrt{\dfrac{37 + 13}{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{25} = 5\]
Why: Put \(|z|\) and \(x\) in \(p = \sqrt{(|z| + x)/2}\).

Work out \(q\)
\[q = \sqrt{\dfrac{37 - 13}{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}\]
Why: Put \(|z|\) and \(x\) in \(q = \sqrt{(|z| - x)/2}\).

Choose the signs
\[\sqrt{13 - 20\sqrt{3}i} = \pm(5 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i)\]
Why: \(y\) is negative, so the \(i\) part takes the opposite sign to the real part.

Check: square the root
\[(5 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i)^2\]
\[= 25 - 20\sqrt{3}\,i + 12i^2\]
\[= 13 - 20\sqrt{3}\,i \;\checkmark\]
Why: Squaring gives back the original number, so both roots are correct (the other root is just the negative).

Plot the roots on an Argand diagram
\[5 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i \to (5,\ -2\sqrt{3})\]
\[-5 + 2\sqrt{3}\,i \to (-5,\ 2\sqrt{3})\]
\[2\sqrt{3} \approx 3.46\]
Why: On an Argand diagram \(a + ib\) is the point \((a, b)\): real part along the \(x\)-axis, imaginary part along the \(y\)-axis. The first root is in quadrant IV, the second in quadrant II; they are opposite each other through \(O\), because one root is the negative of the other.
blocks.final_answer: \(\sqrt{13 - 20\sqrt{3}i} = \pm(5 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i)\): the points \((5, -2\sqrt{3})\) and \((-5, 2\sqrt{3})\) on the Argand diagram

answer_figure.alt: Argand diagram with the real axis horizontal and the imaginary axis vertical, both marked from -6 to 6. Two points are plotted: 5 minus 2 root 3 i at (5, about -3.46) in the fourth quadrant, and -5 plus 2 root 3 i at (-5, about 3.46) in the second quadrant. A dashed line joins them through the origin.
